parole.testo: From Late Latin paradisiăcus, from Byzantine Greek παραδεισιακός (paradeisiakós), from Ancient Greek παράδεισος (parádeisos).

Borrowed from Late Latin patriarcha, from Byzantine Greek πατριάρχης (patriárkhēs, “the founder of the tribe/family”), from Ancient Greek πατριά (patriá, “generation, ancestry, descent, tribe, family”) + -άρχης (-árkhēs, “-arch”).

From Late Latin Rōmaeus, calque of Byzantine Greek ῥωμαῖος (rhōmaîos, literally “Roman”). By surface analysis, Roma + -eo. The “pilgrim” sense comes from a sobriquet given to Roman Catholic pilgrims to the Holy Land.
From Late Latin sclavus (“slave”), from Sclavus (“Slav”), from Byzantine Greek Σκλάβος (Sklábos, “Slav”). Doublet of slavo and ciao. Cognate with Sicilian scavu.
